facts.text: After the Columbia foam strike in January 2003, engineers used the empirical Crater impact model to assess tile damage.
facts.quote: Following the foam strike in January 2003, engineers used the empirical Crater impact model to assess tile damage.

facts.text: In August 2003, the Columbia Accident Investigation Board found in F6.3-10 that the tile-damage assessment used an impact simulation well outside Crater's test database.
facts.quote: The Columbia Accident Investigation Board (August 2003) found (F6.3-10) that the assessment used "an impact simulation that was well outside Crater's test database"

facts.text: The Columbia Accident Investigation Board found in F6.3-10 that the analyst conducting the Crater tile-damage assessment was inexperienced.
facts.quote: and that the analyst was inexperienced

facts.text: The Columbia Accident Investigation Board found in F6.3-11 that Crater predicted penetration deeper than the tile, but engineers used their judgment to conclude that the damage would not penetrate.
facts.quote: (F6.3-11) that Crater predicted penetration deeper than the tile, but engineers "used their judgment" to conclude the damage would not penetrate.

facts.text: The estimated Columbia strike debris was hundreds of times larger than the data used to calibrate Crater: the briefing initially cited 640 times, while later analysis said about 400 times.
facts.quote: The estimated debris was hundreds of times larger than the data used to calibrate the model; the briefing first cited 640 times and later analysis said about 400 times.

facts.text: Crater tended to overpredict penetration in its small-impact calibration data and was regarded as conservative within that domain.
facts.quote: Crater had tended to overpredict penetration in the small-impact calibration data and was regarded as conservative there

facts.text: Crater's conservative bias in small-impact calibration data was extrapolated to the much larger Columbia foam strike.
facts.quote: that conservative bias was extrapolated to the much larger strike

facts.text: The in-flight assessment of the Columbia foam strike reported no safety-of-flight issue.
facts.quote: the in-flight assessment reported no safety-of-flight issue.

facts.text: Columbia was lost on re-entry on 1 February 2003.
facts.quote: Columbia was lost on re-entry on 1 February 2003.

facts.text: The Columbia Accident Investigation Board criticized briefing slides for misrepresenting key information, including vague wording such as "significant" and "significantly".
facts.quote: The Board also criticized the briefing slides for misrepresenting key information, including vague wording such as "significant" and "significantly".

facts.text: In a dissenting 2011 blog account, former Shuttle program manager Wayne Hale argued that Crater actually predicted unsafe damage and that the failure was management overriding the model.
facts.quote: Dissent (former Shuttle program manager Wayne Hale, 2011 blog): Crater actually predicted unsafe damage, and the failure was management overriding it.

facts.text: The Columbia case illustrates two failure modes: using a model outside its validity envelope and human reinterpretation of out-of-envelope results, rather than merely simulation inaccuracy.
facts.quote: Both a model used outside its envelope and human reinterpretation of out-of-envelope results are failure modes.

facts.text: The Columbia case directly drove the creation of NASA-STD-7009.
facts.quote: The case directly drove the creation of NASA-STD-7009

facts.text: NASA's credibility material uses the Columbia case to illustrate giving a model decision weight beyond its credibility.
facts.quote: NASA's credibility material uses it to illustrate giving a model decision weight beyond its credibility.

facts.text: A perception simulation that is conservative in light dust cannot be assumed conservative in dense dust.
facts.quote: a perception simulation that is conservative in light dust cannot be assumed conservative in dense dust

facts.text: A brake model that is conservative on dry compacted soil cannot be assumed conservative on an icy grade.
facts.quote: a brake model conservative on dry compacted soil cannot be assumed conservative on an icy grade

facts.text: A sensor model validated at one installation height cannot be assumed conservative after a large pose change.
facts.quote: a sensor model validated at one installation height cannot be assumed conservative after a large pose change.

facts.text: Model conservatism itself has a validity domain; demonstrated conservative behavior within a validated domain does not establish conservatism outside that domain.
facts.quote: Conservatism itself has a validity domain.
